entities.summary: John of Hauville was a moralist and satirical poet of the 12th century, who gained prominence for his work *De moribus* (On Morals) and *De amicitia* (On Friendship). He was known for his sharp wit and criticism of the nobility, which often found him at odds with the powerful. His satirical writings tackled topics such as the corrupting influence of power and the social ills of the time. He was a key figure in the medieval literary scene, influencing writers such as *Walter Map* and *Geoffrey Chaucer*. His work has been recognized for its insightful commentary on the human condition and the social context of his time. Through his writings, John of Hauville left a lasting legacy that continues to be studied by scholars today.
